rows.description: Five friends list transport, stay, food and entry costs for a Manali trip, add a ten percent cushion, and divide by five to see what each must save.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, contingency planning, groupthink planning, negotiation, working backward

rows.subtype: Approach: working backward from dates and exams [Thinking]
rows.description: Given exam dates and holiday days, the group finds the only free window, then books trains first because the rest depends on it, and fixes stays afterward.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, contingency planning, groupthink planning, negotiation, resource and budget planning

rows.subtype: Approach: a shared expense sheet and advance deposit [Action]
rows.description: The group opens a shared sheet, each puts an initial amount into one account, and every payment is logged, which prevents later arguments about who owes what.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, contingency planning, groupthink planning, negotiation, resource and budget planning, working backward

rows.subtype: Approach: leaving planning to the last moment [Pitfall]
rows.description: The group keeps saying it will figure it out later, so prices rise, trains fill up, and the trip is cut short or dropped, which leaves people disappointed.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, contingency planning, groupthink planning, negotiation, resource and budget planning, working backward

rows.subtype: Approach: pooling ideas then agreeing a shortlist [Thinking]
rows.description: Each friend names two must-do places, the group notices that everything cannot fit in four days, and votes on a compact route that keeps everyone's top pick.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, contingency planning, groupthink planning, negotiation, resource and budget planning, working backward

rows.subtype: Approach: groupthink over an unaffordable plan [Pitfall]
rows.description: Nobody wants to be the one to say the plan is too costly, so a member with a tight allowance silently agrees, then struggles to pay and feels excluded.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, contingency planning, negotiation, resource and budget planning, working backward

rows.subtype: Approach: contingency planning for weather and delays [Thinking]
rows.description: The group prepares for landslides or delayed buses with a spare day, refundable bookings where possible, and a list of indoor options.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, groupthink planning, negotiation, resource and budget planning, working backward

rows.description: The group agrees openly that a friend on a smaller allowance takes a cheaper room option, while shared costs like cabs are split equally, so nobody is embarrassed.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, contingency planning, groupthink planning, resource and budget planning, working backward

rows.subtype: Approach: informing parents with itinerary and contacts [Action]
rows.description: Each friend shares the itinerary, stay address and a contact number with their family, and keeps live location on for the group, which builds trust and safety.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, contingency planning, groupthink planning, negotiation, resource and budget planning, working backward

rows.subtype: Approach: replanning when money runs short mid-trip [Revision]
rows.description: On day two the group sees spending is higher than planned, so they skip a paid activity, cook one meal, and choose free viewpoints instead of dropping the trip.
